claims.text: Machine-learning interatomic potentials will improve representation of atomic configurations in ab initio liquids of multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Improved representation of atomic configurations will produce better phase-space overlap between the reference and ab initio target systems.
Machine-learning interatomic potentials will improve representation of local order parameters.
Better phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The thermodynamic-integration path mismatch will be reduced by at least 20% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
Reduced thermodynamic-integration path mismatch will result in more accurate predictions of thermodynamic properties.
TOR-TILD uses EAM reference potentials as the relevant baseline.
The proposed method applies to high-entropy alloys containing three to six principal elements.
The proposed method applies over temperatures from 0.8 to 1.2 times the melting temperature.
The proposed method applies to both solid and liquid states at and near high melting temperatures.
The accuracy of machine-learning interatomic potentials may depend on training-data quality and alloy-system complexity.
A reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch of less than 10% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts and defines success as at least a 20% reduction, but falsification requires a reduction below 10%. Results from 10% through less than 20% would fail the stated hypothesis while not satisfying its falsification rule, leaving the benchmark non-decisive.
